whyWrongByChoice.D: Recipient natural killer cells are not the described mediator of GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Donor plasma cells produce antibody; GVHD injury results from donor T-cell cytotoxicity and cytokine release, not humoral immunity.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with diabetic nephropathy receives a kidney transplant. Intraoperatively the surgeon notes the organ is pale and poorly perfused; a thrombus has formed and is preventing perfusion of the graft. Which type of rejection is most likely?

explanation.summary: Rejection occurring within minutes of transplantation is hyperacute.
explanation.whyCorrect: The type of rejection described is hyperacute because it occurred within minutes of transplantation, with thrombosis and poor perfusion caused by pre-formed antibodies activating complement on the graft endothelium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute rejection occurs about one week to several months after the transplant, not intraoperatively.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic rejection occurs months to years later and manifests as graft arteriosclerosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Graft-versus-host disease occurs weeks to months after transplant and results mainly from bone marrow transplant, not from an immediate kidney thrombosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Subacute rejection is not one of the recognized categories of transplant rejection described in the brick.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 39-year-old kidney transplant recipient develops rising creatinine 6 weeks after surgery. Biopsy shows inflammatory cells infiltrating between the epithelial cells of the tubules (tubulitis) and CD8+ T cells destroying graft cells. Which of the following best describes this process?

explanation.summary: Tubulitis with CD8+ T-cell-mediated graft cell killing defines acute cellular rejection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute cellular rejection occurs when CD8+ T cells directly destroy graft cells or CD4+ T cells secrete cytokines and induce inflammation. On kidney biopsy it manifests as tubulitis, with inflammatory cells between the epithelial cells of the tubules, matching this patient's findings weeks after transplant.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Acute antibody-mediated rejection involves antibodies binding endothelium with complement activation and shows C4d deposition and capillaritis, not primarily T-cell tubulitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyperacute rejection occurs within minutes to 24 hours and shows thrombosis, not a T-cell tubulitis weeks later.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chronic rejection develops over months to years with graft arteriosclerosis and fibrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GVHD involves donor T cells attacking recipient tissue and is characteristic of bone marrow, not kidney, transplants.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 60-year-old kidney transplant recipient has worsening graft function 2 months post-transplant. Biopsy shows peritubular capillaritis, and an immunoperoxidase stain reveals C4d deposition in peritubular capillaries. Which mechanism is most likely responsible?

choices.label: B
choices.text: IgE-mediated release of mast cell mediators

choices.label: C
choices.text: Donor T cells attacking recipient endothelium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intimal smooth muscle proliferation occluding vessels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Direct CD8+ T-cell killing of tubular cells

explanation.summary: C4d deposition marks acute antibody-mediated rejection.
explanation.whyCorrect: In acute antibody-mediated rejection, antibodies bind to vascular endothelium and activate complement; the resulting inflammation and endothelial damage cause graft failure. The complement split product C4d deposited in peritubular capillaries, demonstrated by immunoperoxidase staining, is the diagnostic marker.

whyWrongByChoice.B: IgE and mast cell mediators drive type I hypersensitivity, not complement-fixing antibody rejection of a graft.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Donor T cells attacking the recipient describe GVHD, not antibody-mediated rejection of a kidney graft.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intimal proliferation with vessel occlusion is a feature of chronic rejection, not C4d-positive antibody-mediated injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Direct CD8+ T-cell killing describes acute cellular rejection with tubulitis, which is not marked by C4d deposition.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man who received a heart transplant 4 years ago develops progressive graft dysfunction. Angiography shows diffuse narrowing of the coronary arteries, and biopsy reveals graft arteriosclerosis with intimal smooth muscle proliferation. Which type of rejection does this represent?

explanation.summary: Graft arteriosclerosis developing years after transplant is chronic rejection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic rejection can occur months to years after transplant and involves both cellular and humoral immune responses. It produces graft arteriosclerosis, with intimal smooth muscle proliferation and vessel occlusion, plus interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy, matching the coronary narrowing years after a heart transplant.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hyperacute rejection occurs within minutes to 24 hours with thrombosis, not slowly progressive arteriosclerosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acute cellular rejection occurs within weeks to months and shows T-cell tubulitis or endothelitis, not chronic arteriosclerosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Acute antibody-mediated rejection occurs within weeks to months with C4d deposition, not years-long vascular remodeling.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GVHD is a bone marrow transplant complication in which donor cells attack the recipient, not chronic coronary graft arteriosclerosis.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman develops anaphylaxis after a bee sting, with hypotension, urticaria, and bronchospasm. This reaction is mediated by IgE causing release of mast cell mediators. Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is this, and which type of transplant rejection shares the antibody-mediated category most analogous to hyperacute rejection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Type I hypersensitivity; hyperacute rejection is type II

choices.label: B
choices.text: Type II hypersensitivity; hyperacute rejection is type I

choices.label: C
choices.text: Type III hypersensitivity; hyperacute rejection is type IV

choices.label: D
choices.text: Type IV hypersensitivity; hyperacute rejection is type III

choices.label: E
choices.text: Type I hypersensitivity; hyperacute rejection is type IV

explanation.summary: Anaphylaxis is type I; hyperacute rejection is a type II (antibody-mediated) reaction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type I hypersensitivity is immediate, mediated by IgE antibodies that trigger release of mast cell mediators, producing anaphylaxis, allergies, and bronchial asthma. Hyperacute rejection, caused by pre-formed antibodies activating complement against graft endothelium, is classified as a type II hypersensitivity reaction.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Anaphylaxis is not type II; type II involves IgG/IgM injuring cells, and hyperacute rejection is type II, not type I.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anaphylaxis is not type III (immune-complex); hyperacute rejection is not type IV.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anaphylaxis is not type IV (T-cell mediated); hyperacute rejection is not type III.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anaphylaxis is correctly type I, but hyperacute rejection is type II, not type IV.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man develops an intensely pruritic, vesicular rash 48 hours after his skin contacts poison ivy. Biopsy shows a T-cell-rich infiltrate with macrophage activation and no antibody deposition. Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is responsible?

explanation.summary: Contact dermatitis is a delayed, T-cell-mediated type IV hypersensitivity reaction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type IV hypersensitivity reactions occur when T cells cause either direct cytotoxicity (CD8+ T cells) or induce inflammation and cytokine release (CD4+ T cells) with macrophage activation. Examples include contact dermatitis, type I diabetes, and graft-versus-host disease, consistent with this delayed poison ivy reaction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Type I is IgE-mediated and immediate (anaphylaxis, allergy), not a delayed T-cell reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Type II involves IgG or IgM injuring cells by phagocytosis or lysis, not T-cell contact dermatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Type III involves immune-complex deposition (e.g., lupus, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis), not cell-mediated contact dermatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Type V is not among the four hypersensitivity categories described in the brick.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A hematologist is counseling a patient before an allogeneic bone marrow transplant about the risk of graft-versus-host disease. Which of the following best explains why GVHD develops in this setting but is rare after solid organ transplants such as kidney?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone marrow transplant tissue contains abundant donor T cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: The recipient's pre-formed antibodies react against donor marrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recipient CD8+ T cells reject the donor marrow

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immune complexes deposit in the recipient's bone marrow

choices.label: E
choices.text: Donor IgE triggers mast cell degranulation in the recipient

explanation.summary: GVHD occurs because bone marrow grafts are rich in donor T cells that recognize recipient tissue as foreign.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bone marrow transplant tissue typically contains a large number of T cells. Unlike graft rejection, in which the recipient's immune cells recognize the graft as foreign, in GVHD the donor's transplanted T cells recognize the recipient's tissues as foreign and attack the recipient's organs, causing severe organ dysfunction. This is why GVHD is characteristic of allogeneic bone marrow, not solid organ, transplants.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Pre-formed recipient antibodies against a graft cause hyperacute rejection, not GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Recipient CD8+ T cells rejecting the graft describes host-versus-graft rejection, the opposite of GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immune-complex deposition is a type III hypersensitivity mechanism, not the basis of GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Donor IgE and mast cells describe type I hypersensitivity, which does not mediate GVHD.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman with GVHD after bone marrow transplant develops jaundice with a rising direct bilirubin. Which of the following histopathologic changes best accounts for her jaundice?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Patchy epithelial cell death in the epidermis

explanation.summary: Jaundice in GVHD results from immune destruction of small bile ducts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with GVHD may present with jaundice caused by destruction of the small bile ducts, which impairs bile flow and raises bilirubin. This reflects donor T-cell-mediated attack on recipient hepatic tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Mucosal ulceration of the gut causes the diarrhea of GVHD, not jaundice.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Patchy epidermal cell death produces the maculopapular skin rash of GVHD, not jaundice.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Graft arteriosclerosis is a feature of chronic solid-organ rejection, not the cause of GVHD-related jaundice.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Platelet-fibrin thrombi characterize hyperacute rejection of a solid organ graft, not GVHD hepatic injury.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man is being evaluated for a bone marrow transplant and asks about his risk of graft-versus-host disease. Which of the following is a recognized risk factor for developing GVHD?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Young donor age with fully matched HLA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Complete depletion of donor T cells from the graft

explanation.summary: GVHD occurs most frequently in recipients exposed to radiation or with leukemia, autoimmune disease, or immunodeficiency.
explanation.whyCorrect: GVHD occurs most frequently in recipients who have been exposed to radiation or who have leukemia, autoimmune diseases, or immunodeficiencies. Other contributing factors include transplantation from female donors to male recipients. Some of this risk relates to immunosuppression of the recipient, reducing the ability to neutralize the donor T-lymphocyte attack.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A young, fully HLA-matched donor reduces rather than increases the alloreactivity that drives GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Recipients are typically conditioned with chemotherapy to eradicate marrow; absence of chemotherapy is not a listed GVHD risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GVHD requires an allogeneic (non-identical donor) graft; autologous transplants use the patient's own cells and do not cause GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Depleting donor T cells removes the very cells that mediate GVHD, lowering the risk.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A transplant team manages a kidney recipient on multiple immunosuppressive drugs. The team notes that standardized histologic criteria are used to diagnose and grade rejection across organs. Which criteria are used specifically for grading rejection in kidney transplants?

explanation.summary: The Banff criteria are used to grade kidney transplant rejection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Several histologic criteria have been created to diagnose and grade rejection for organ transplants. The Banff criteria are used for kidney transplants, while the ISHLT criteria are applied to heart transplants.

whyWrongByChoice.B: ISHLT criteria are used for heart transplant rejection, not kidney.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ranson criteria assess the severity of acute pancreatitis, not transplant rejection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Child-Pugh criteria grade chronic liver disease severity, not graft rejection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TNM staging describes cancer extent, not transplant rejection grading.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease is evaluated for kidney transplantation. She has had four pregnancies and received multiple blood transfusions during a prior surgery. The transplant team warns that she is at increased risk of hyperacute rejection. Which of the following best explains her elevated risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic immunosuppression from her prior surgery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prior exposure that induced antibodies against MHC molecules

choices.label: C
choices.text: Expansion of alloreactive CD8+ T cells during pregnancy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deposition of immune complexes in her native kidneys

choices.label: E
choices.text: Acquired IgE sensitization to donor blood group antigens

explanation.summary: Prior transfusion, pregnancy, or transplantation can induce anti-MHC antibodies that cause hyperacute rejection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hyperacute rejection depends on pre-formed recipient antibodies. Besides natural IgM against blood group antigens, these may be antibodies specific for MHC molecules that were induced by prior exposure to foreign cells through blood transfusion, pregnancy, or transplantation of another organ. Her history of pregnancies and transfusions makes such antibodies likely.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immunosuppression would reduce, not increase, an antibody-mediated response, and surgery does not cause chronic immunosuppression.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyperacute rejection is antibody mediated (type 2 hypersensitivity), not driven by CD8+ T cells, which mediate acute cellular rejection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immune-complex deposition is a type III hypersensitivity mechanism and is not the basis of hyperacute rejection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IgE mediates type I hypersensitivity; hyperacute rejection involves IgM or anti-MHC antibodies that activate complement.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 57-year-old man undergoes kidney transplantation. Within 30 minutes of reperfusion the graft becomes cyanotic and mottled, and a frozen section shows fibrin-platelet thrombi in glomerular capillaries with ischemic necrosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Perform a repeat biopsy in 48 hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove the graft as soon as possible

explanation.summary: A hyperacutely rejected graft must be removed as soon as possible.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is hyperacute rejection: pre-formed antibodies against ABO or class I MHC antigens on graft endothelium trigger the complement cascade, producing thrombosis, ischemia, and necrosis within minutes to 24 hours. Because the graft is already irreversibly infarcting, it must be removed as soon as possible.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immunosuppressive medication treats acute rejection, which responds to it; it cannot reverse complement-mediated thrombosis of an already necrotic graft.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Waiting 48 hours for another biopsy delays removal of a necrotic organ that cannot be salvaged.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The process is antibody and complement mediated, not infectious, so antibiotics do not address it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Observation is inappropriate; the graft has undergone ischemic necrosis and requires removal.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man with no history of blood transfusion, prior transplantation, or pregnancy-related exposure receives a kidney from a donor of a different ABO blood group. Minutes after anastomosis the graft thromboses. Which of the following antibodies most likely mediated this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Natural IgM antibodies against a blood group antigen

choices.label: B
choices.text: IgG antibodies induced against class II MHC molecules

choices.label: C
choices.text: IgE antibodies against donor endothelial proteins

choices.label: D
choices.text: IgA antibodies deposited in glomerular mesangium

explanation.summary: Natural IgM antibodies against ABO blood group antigens cause hyperacute rejection without any prior sensitization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hyperacute rejection results from pre-formed recipient antibodies that react against ABO blood group antigens or class I MHC molecules on graft endothelial cells. In a patient with no prior sensitizing exposure, the pre-formed antibodies are natural IgM antibodies against a blood group antigen, which exist without prior transfusion, pregnancy, or transplantation and explain the reaction after an ABO-mismatched graft.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Anti-MHC antibodies require induction by prior exposure (transfusion, pregnancy, transplantation), which this patient lacks; the brick names class I MHC, not class II, as the endothelial target.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgE mediates type I hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis, allergy), not the complement-fixing type 2 reaction of hyperacute rejection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IgA mesangial deposition is not the mechanism of graft thrombosis within minutes of transplantation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hyperacute rejection is caused by the recipient's antibodies against the graft, not donor antibodies against the recipient.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with hemoptysis and hematuria. Renal biopsy shows IgG antibodies bound along the glomerular basement membrane, and he is diagnosed with Goodpasture syndrome. Which of the following mechanisms of hypersensitivity is responsible for his tissue injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IgE-triggered release of mast cell mediators

choices.label: C
choices.text: IgG or IgM antibodies injuring cells and inducing inflammation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Direct cytotoxicity by CD8+ T cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cytokine release and macrophage activation by CD4+ T cells

explanation.summary: Goodpasture syndrome is a type II hypersensitivity reaction mediated by IgG or IgM antibodies against cells and tissues.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type II hypersensitivity reactions occur when IgG and IgM antibodies injure cells by promoting their phagocytosis or lysis and induce inflammation. Examples cited include autoimmune hemolytic anemia and Goodpasture syndrome, in which antibody bound to the basement membrane produces the inflammation and injury.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IgE and mast cell mediators characterize type I hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis, allergies, bronchial asthma), not Goodpasture syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immune-complex deposition is type III hypersensitivity, exemplified by lupus and post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, not antibody bound directly to tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CD8+ T-cell cytotoxicity is a type IV mechanism seen in contact dermatitis, type I diabetes, and GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CD4+ T-cell cytokine release with macrophage activation is the other arm of type IV hypersensitivity, not an antibody-mediated process.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: An 8-year-old boy develops periorbital edema, hypertension, and cola-colored urine 2 weeks after an untreated episode of pharyngitis. He is diagnosed with post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of glomerular injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IgE antibodies causing mast cell degranulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: IgG antibodies promoting phagocytosis of glomerular cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: CD8+ T cells directly killing glomerular epithelial cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: CD4+ T cells activating macrophages within the glomerulus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Antigen-antibody complexes deposited in tissue inducing inflammation

explanation.summary: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is a type III hypersensitivity reaction caused by immune-complex deposition.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type III hypersensitivity reactions occur when antigen-antibody complexes (IgG or IgM) are deposited in tissues and induce inflammation and tissue damage. The brick lists lupus and post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis as the examples of this mechanism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation is type I hypersensitivity, seen in anaphylaxis, allergies, and bronchial asthma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibodies directly injuring cells by promoting phagocytosis or lysis is type II hypersensitivity, as in autoimmune hemolytic anemia and Goodpasture syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Direct CD8+ T-cell cytotoxicity is a type IV mechanism, not the basis of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CD4+ T-cell cytokine release with macrophage activation is type IV hypersensitivity, exemplified by contact dermatitis and GVHD.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman with bronchial asthma develops wheezing and chest tightness minutes after exposure to cat dander. Her airway narrowing results from the action of mast cell mediators released in a type I hypersensitivity reaction. On which of the following targets do these mediators act to produce her symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glomerular basement membrane and tubular epithelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood vessels and smooth muscle cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endothelial cells bearing class I MHC molecules

choices.label: D
choices.text: Macrophages and neutrophils in the interstitium

explanation.summary: Type I hypersensitivity mediators act on vessels and smooth muscle, producing vasodilation, edema, smooth muscle contraction, and mucus production.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type I hypersensitivity reactions are immediate; IgE antibodies cause release of mast cell mediators, and these mediators act on vessels and smooth muscle cells to produce vasodilation, edema, smooth muscle contraction, and mucus production. Bronchial asthma, anaphylaxis, and allergies are the examples given, and bronchial smooth muscle contraction with mucus production explains her wheezing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glomerular basement membrane injury is a target of antibody in type II reactions such as Goodpasture syndrome, not of mast cell mediators.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endothelial class I MHC molecules are the target of pre-formed antibodies in hyperacute rejection, a type 2 reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Recruitment of macrophages and neutrophils by cytokines is the CD4+ T-cell arm of type IV hypersensitivity and acute cellular rejection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Parenchymal cells bearing alloantigens are killed by CD8+ T cells in acute cellular rejection, not affected by mast cell mediators.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman develops a diffuse maculopapular rash, profuse diarrhea, and rising bilirubin 4 weeks after an allogeneic bone marrow transplant. Skin biopsy shows patchy epithelial cell death, yet the pathologist notes that the tissue is not heavily infiltrated by lymphocytes. Which of the following best explains the severity of tissue injury despite the sparse infiltrate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complement fixation by pre-formed recipient antibodies

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immune-complex deposition along the dermal-epidermal junction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intimal smooth muscle proliferation in dermal arterioles

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cytokine release in addition to direct CD8+ T-cell cytotoxicity

choices.label: E
choices.text: IgE-triggered mast cell degranulation within the dermis

explanation.summary: GVHD injury is believed to result from cytokine release plus direct CD8+ T-cell cytotoxicity, so tissues need not be heavily infiltrated.
explanation.whyCorrect: In GVHD, although tissue injury can be severe, affected tissues are not usually heavily infiltrated by lymphocytes. It is believed that damage is caused by cytokine release in addition to direct cytotoxicity by donor CD8+ T cells, consistent with the type IV (T-cell mediated) nature of GVHD.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pre-formed recipient antibodies activating complement cause hyperacute rejection of a solid organ, not GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immune-complex deposition is a type III hypersensitivity mechanism, not the cell-mediated injury of GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intimal smooth muscle proliferation is the vascular lesion of chronic rejection (graft arteriosclerosis), not GVHD skin injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation is type I hypersensitivity and does not explain T-cell-driven epithelial cell death.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man has a rising serum creatinine 3 weeks after kidney transplantation. Biopsy shows interstitial inflammatory cells infiltrating between tubular epithelial cells. The graft is still well perfused. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

explanation.summary: Acute rejection is the principal cause of early graft failure and responds to immunosuppressive medication.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tubulitis 3 weeks after transplant is acute cellular rejection. Acute rejection occurs 1 week to several months after transplant, is the principal cause of early graft failure, and responds to immunosuppressive medication, so the appropriate step is to treat with intensified immunosuppression rather than abandon the graft.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Immediate graft removal is the management of hyperacute rejection, in which the graft is thrombosed and necrotic; acute rejection is treatable.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Withdrawing immunosuppression would allow the T-cell attack on the graft to accelerate and hasten graft failure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The biopsy shows rejection, not infection; antibiotics do not treat T-cell mediated tubulitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Untreated acute rejection is the principal cause of early graft failure; observation alone risks losing the graft.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman has worsening graft function 5 weeks after kidney transplantation. Biopsy shows an arteriole in which inflammatory cells are attacking and undermining the endothelium (endothelitis), together with interstitial inflammation. Immunoperoxidase staining for C4d in peritubular capillaries is negative. Which of the following best describes the process?

explanation.summary: Rejection vasculitis (endothelitis) with a negative C4d stain is acute cellular (T-cell mediated) rejection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute cellular rejection is mediated by CD8+ T cells directly destroying graft cells and CD4+ T cells secreting cytokines that induce inflammation. In a kidney graft it manifests as tubulitis and as rejection vasculitis, in which inflammatory cells attack and undermine the endothelium of an arteriole (endothelitis). The absence of C4d deposition argues against an antibody-mediated process.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hyperacute rejection occurs within minutes to 24 hours and shows platelet-fibrin thrombi and ischemic necrosis, not T-cell endothelitis weeks later.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acute antibody-mediated rejection is marked by capillaritis with C4d deposition in peritubular capillaries; the negative C4d stain excludes it here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chronic rejection develops months to years later with intimal smooth muscle proliferation, interstitial fibrosis, and tubular atrophy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GVHD involves donor T cells attacking recipient tissue after bone marrow transplant and does not cause vasculitis of a kidney graft.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A pathologist examines a kidney graft biopsy showing acute cellular rejection. In addition to CD8+ T cells directly killing parenchymal cells, alloantigen-specific CD4+ T cells are contributing to interstitial inflammation. Which of the following cells are recruited to the graft by the cytokines these CD4+ T cells secrete?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vascular smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts

explanation.summary: In acute cellular rejection, CD4+ T-cell cytokines recruit macrophages and neutrophils that cause interstitial inflammation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute T-cell mediated rejection involves direct killing of graft cells by CD8+ T cells and inflammation caused by cytokines produced by CD4+ T cells. Those cytokines recruit macrophages and neutrophils, which together with parenchymal cell damage produce the interstitial inflammation seen on biopsy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Plasma cells and mast cells are not the effector cells recruited by CD4+ T-cell cytokines in acute cellular rejection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Platelets contribute to the fibrin-platelet thrombi of hyperacute rejection, not to T-cell mediated interstitial inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Natural killer cells and eosinophils are not described as the recruited inflammatory cells in acute cellular rejection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vascular smooth muscle proliferation is the intimal lesion of chronic rejection, not an acute recruited inflammatory infiltrate.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman is preparing to be discharged after an uncomplicated kidney transplant. She is currently taking five immunosuppressive drugs and asks how long she will need medication to prevent rejection. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All immunosuppressive drugs can be stopped once the graft is functioning at 1 year

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most recipients need two to three drugs throughout their lifespan

choices.label: C
choices.text: A single drug is sufficient after the first month

choices.label: D
choices.text: Four or more drugs must be continued for life

choices.label: E
choices.text: Drugs are required only if a rejection episode occurs

explanation.summary: Transplant recipients typically take four or more drugs early on and two to three drugs lifelong to prevent rejection.
explanation.whyCorrect: It is common for transplant recipients to be taking four or more immunosuppressive drugs in the days immediately after surgery. Most recipients then require two to three drugs throughout their lifespan to prevent rejection, including chronic rejection, which immunosuppressive drugs act to prevent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immunosuppression is not stopped after a year; chronic rejection can occur months to years later and is prevented by ongoing drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brick states most recipients require two to three drugs, not one, for life.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Four or more drugs are typical only in the days immediately after surgery, not lifelong.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immunosuppressive drugs are given continuously to prevent rejection, not only reactively after rejection begins.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man who received a kidney transplant 8 months ago presents with fever, cough, and a new pulmonary infiltrate. He is taking three immunosuppressive drugs and has had no rejection episodes. Which of the following best explains his susceptibility to this illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Donor T cells attacking his respiratory epithelium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immunosuppressive drugs suppressing his immune system

explanation.summary: Immunosuppressive drugs prevent rejection but place transplant recipients at risk for infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most transplant recipients require two to three immunosuppressive drugs throughout their lifespan to prevent rejection. These drugs suppress the immune system, so patients are at risk for infections, which explains his pneumonia in the absence of any rejection episode.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Donor T cells attacking recipient tissue is GVHD, which is characteristic of bone marrow, not kidney, transplants.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pre-formed antibodies activating complement cause hyperacute rejection of the graft within 24 hours, not a lung infection months later.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Graft arteriosclerosis of chronic rejection affects the transplanted organ's vessels, not the lungs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immune-complex deposition is a type III hypersensitivity mechanism and does not explain infectious susceptibility.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman who received a kidney transplant 6 years ago has slowly rising creatinine and proteinuria. Biopsy shows inflammatory cells within glomerular capillary loops, accumulation of mesangial matrix, and duplication of the glomerular capillary basement membrane, along with interstitial fibrosis. Which of the following best describes this process?

explanation.summary: Glomerulitis with mesangial matrix accumulation, basement membrane duplication, and interstitial fibrosis years after transplant is chronic rejection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic rejection occurs months to years after transplant and involves both cellular and humoral immune responses. In a kidney graft it produces glomerulitis, with inflammatory cells within the capillary loops, accumulation of mesangial matrix, and duplication of the capillary basement membrane, plus interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy, in addition to graft arteriosclerosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Acute cellular rejection occurs 1 week to several months after transplant and shows tubulitis and endothelitis, not basement membrane duplication and fibrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyperacute rejection occurs within 24 hours with platelet-fibrin thrombi and ischemic necrosis of the glomerulus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Acute antibody-mediated rejection presents within weeks to months with peritubular capillaritis and C4d deposition, not years-long glomerular remodeling.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GVHD is a complication of bone marrow transplant in which donor T cells attack recipient organs, not a lesion of a kidney graft.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 53-year-old man with a kidney transplant performed 5 years ago undergoes biopsy for progressive graft dysfunction. A trichrome-stained section shows large blue-staining areas surrounding shrunken tubules, contrasting with adjacent normal-appearing parenchyma. Which of the following do the blue areas represent?

explanation.summary: In chronic rejection, trichrome stain highlights interstitial fibrosis (blue) accompanying tubular atrophy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic rejection, occurring months to years after transplant, produces interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy. On a trichrome stain the blue area shows fibrosis, contrasted with the normal kidney, and the shrunken tubules within it represent tubular atrophy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Platelet-fibrin thrombi are the glomerular lesion of hyperacute rejection within 24 hours, not a years-later interstitial change.
whyWrongByChoice.B: C4d deposition is demonstrated by immunoperoxidase staining of peritubular capillaries in acute antibody-mediated rejection, not by trichrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tubulitis is an inflammatory cell infiltrate between tubular epithelial cells in acute cellular rejection, not a blue collagen-rich area.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mesangial matrix accumulation is a glomerular feature of chronic rejection, not the interstitial blue-staining region around tubules.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 58-year-old heart transplant recipient develops diffuse concentric narrowing of the coronary arteries 3 years after transplantation. Histology shows chronic inflammation in the vessel wall with intimal smooth muscle proliferation and vessel occlusion. Which of the following best describes the pathogenesis of this vascular lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pre-formed IgM antibodies triggering intravascular thrombosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Donor T cells recognizing recipient vascular tissue as foreign

choices.label: C
choices.text: IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation in the adventitia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Circulating immune complexes lodging in the vessel wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cytokines from alloreactive T cells and antibody binding to endothelial antigens

explanation.summary: Graft arteriosclerosis in chronic rejection is driven by T-cell cytokines together with antibody deposition on the endothelium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic rejection involves both cellular and humoral immune responses. Graft arteriosclerosis is caused by cytokines from alloantigen-specific CD4+ T cells and antibody binding to endothelial antigens, producing a chronic inflammatory reaction in the vessel wall, intimal smooth muscle proliferation, and vessel occlusion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pre-formed antibodies triggering thrombosis cause hyperacute rejection within minutes to 24 hours, not intimal proliferation years later.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Donor T cells attacking recipient tissue is the mechanism of GVHD after bone marrow transplant, not chronic rejection of a solid organ.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgE and mast cells mediate type I hypersensitivity and play no role in graft arteriosclerosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immune-complex deposition is a type III mechanism; chronic rejection involves direct antibody binding to endothelial antigens plus T-cell cytokines.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 49-year-old man underwent heart transplantation 3 months ago. A surveillance endomyocardial biopsy is obtained to assess for rejection. Which of the following standardized histologic criteria are used to diagnose and grade rejection in this organ?

explanation.summary: ISHLT criteria grade rejection in heart transplants; Banff criteria are for kidney transplants.
explanation.whyCorrect: Several histologic criteria have been created to diagnose and grade rejection for organ transplants. The ISHLT criteria are applied to heart transplants, whereas the Banff criteria are used for kidney transplants.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Banff criteria grade rejection in kidney transplants, not heart transplants.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Duke criteria are used to diagnose infective endocarditis, not transplant rejection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Jones criteria are used to diagnose acute rheumatic fever, not graft rejection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Light's criteria distinguish transudative from exudative pleural effusions, not rejection grading.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A medical student is asked to classify the forms of transplant rejection by whether antibodies contribute to graft injury. Which of the following is mediated by T cells without an antibody component?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rejection due to natural anti-ABO antibodies

explanation.summary: Acute cellular rejection is purely T-cell mediated; hyperacute, acute antibody-mediated, and chronic rejection all involve antibodies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute cellular rejection occurs when CD8+ T cells directly destroy graft cells or CD4+ T cells secrete cytokines and induce inflammation; no antibody is involved. In contrast, hyperacute rejection is caused by pre-formed antibodies, acute antibody-mediated rejection by antibodies binding endothelium and activating complement, and chronic rejection involves both cellular and humoral responses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hyperacute rejection is caused by pre-formed recipient antibodies against ABO or class I MHC antigens activating complement.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic rejection involves both cellular and humoral immune responses, with antibody deposition contributing to graft arteriosclerosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acute antibody-mediated rejection is by definition antibody driven, with C4d deposition in peritubular capillaries.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Natural IgM antibodies against blood group antigens mediate hyperacute rejection, an antibody-dependent process.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 40-year-old kidney transplant recipient develops graft dysfunction 7 weeks after surgery. Biopsy shows inflammatory cells between tubular epithelial cells and, in a separate area, peritubular capillaritis with strong C4d deposition on immunoperoxidase staining. Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute cellular and acute antibody-mediated rejection are both present

choices.label: B
choices.text: The C4d staining indicates hyperacute rejection superimposed on tubulitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tubulitis excludes an antibody-mediated process, so C4d is an artifact

choices.label: D
choices.text: The findings represent early chronic rejection with humoral features

choices.label: E
choices.text: The pattern indicates graft-versus-host disease of the transplanted kidney

explanation.summary: Acute rejection has two patterns, cellular and antibody-mediated, and most patterns may coexist in a given patient.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute rejection occurs 1 week to several months after transplant via both cell-mediated (T-cell) and antibody-mediated (B-cell) mechanisms. It is divided into acute cellular rejection (tubulitis from T-cell attack) and acute antibody-mediated rejection (capillaritis with C4d deposition), but most patterns may be present in a given patient, so this biopsy shows both processes simultaneously.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hyperacute rejection occurs within minutes to 24 hours with thrombosis and necrosis, not at 7 weeks with capillaritis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The two acute patterns are not mutually exclusive; C4d deposition is the diagnostic marker of antibody-mediated rejection, not an artifact.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chronic rejection develops months to years later with graft arteriosclerosis, interstitial fibrosis, and tubular atrophy, none of which are described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GVHD occurs when donor T cells attack the recipient after bone marrow transplant and is rare after solid organ transplants.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with acute myeloid leukemia is scheduled for an allogeneic bone marrow transplant. He asks why he must receive chemotherapy before the healthy donor marrow is infused. Which of the following is the best explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To deplete T cells from the donor graft before infusion

choices.label: B
choices.text: To remove pre-formed antibodies that could cause hyperacute rejection

choices.label: C
choices.text: To eradicate his own marrow, removing cancerous cells and providing a clean slate

choices.label: D
choices.text: To induce tolerance in the donor T cells toward his tissues

choices.label: E
choices.text: To prevent graft arteriosclerosis in marrow sinusoids

explanation.summary: Recipient marrow is eradicated with chemotherapy to remove cancerous cells and provide a clean slate for the allogeneic graft.
explanation.whyCorrect: In an allogeneic bone marrow transplant, bone marrow cells from a non-identical donor are transplanted into a recipient whose bone marrow has been eradicated with chemotherapy to remove cancerous cells and provide a clean slate for the transplant. As the case discussion notes, it is important to wipe out the cancer cells from the patient's marrow before giving the donor's healthy marrow.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chemotherapy is given to the recipient to eradicate his marrow; it is not a method of removing T cells from the donor graft.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hyperacute rejection from pre-formed antibodies is a solid organ phenomenon; conditioning chemotherapy is aimed at the recipient's marrow, not antibodies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chemotherapy does not induce tolerance in donor T cells; GVHD risk is mitigated afterward with immunosuppressive drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Graft arteriosclerosis is a lesion of chronic solid organ rejection and is unrelated to pre-transplant conditioning.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man with leukemia is preparing for an allogeneic bone marrow transplant. Several relatives are being evaluated as potential donors. Independent of HLA matching, which of the following donor-recipient combinations is a recognized contributing factor for graft-versus-host disease?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Donor of the same ABO blood group as the recipient

explanation.summary: Transplantation from a female donor to a male recipient is a contributing factor for GVHD.
explanation.whyCorrect: GVHD occurs most frequently in recipients who have been exposed to radiation or who have leukemia, autoimmune diseases, or immunodeficiencies. Other contributing factors include transplantation from female donors to male recipients, making this pairing the recognized risk among those listed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Male-to-male transplantation is not the sex-mismatch pairing identified as a contributing factor for GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The brick identifies female donor to male recipient, not male donor to female recipient, as the contributing factor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: ABO compatibility relates to hyperacute rejection of solid organs; it is not described as a GVHD risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Donor age relative to the recipient is not listed as a contributing factor for GVHD.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man with a congenital immunodeficiency receives an allogeneic bone marrow transplant and develops severe graft-versus-host disease. His physician explains that his underlying immunodeficiency increased his risk. Which of the following best explains this relationship?

choices.label: A
choices.text: His deficient immune system produced excess pre-formed anti-donor antibodies

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immunosuppression of the recipient reduced his ability to neutralize the donor T-lymphocyte attack

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immunodeficiency increased the number of T cells contained in the donor marrow

choices.label: D
choices.text: His immunodeficiency caused the donor marrow to undergo hyperacute rejection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Immunodeficiency promoted immune-complex deposition in his skin and gut

explanation.summary: Immunosuppressed recipients are less able to neutralize the attack by donor T lymphocytes, increasing GVHD risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: GVHD occurs most frequently in recipients exposed to radiation or with leukemia, autoimmune diseases, or immunodeficiencies. Some of these risk factors may be due to immunosuppression of the recipient, leading to a decrease in the ability of the recipient to neutralize the T-lymphocyte attack from the donor, so the donor T cells attack his organs unopposed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: GVHD is mediated by donor T cells, not recipient antibodies, and an immunodeficient recipient would not overproduce antibodies.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The T-cell content of the donor marrow is a property of the graft and is not altered by the recipient's immune status.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hyperacute rejection is a recipient antibody attack on a solid organ graft; GVHD is the reverse direction and involves donor T cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immune-complex deposition is a type III hypersensitivity mechanism; GVHD is a type IV, T-cell mediated reaction.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman is 3 weeks post allogeneic bone marrow transplant. She develops a maculopapular rash, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain with diarrhea, and hepatosplenomegaly with rising bilirubin. Which of the following sets of organs is characteristically involved when GVHD symptoms appear within weeks of transplant?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bone marrow, thymus, and lymph nodes

explanation.summary: Early GVHD characteristically targets the skin, liver, and gastrointestinal tract.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with GVHD may present with a maculopapular rash, jaundice from destruction of small bile ducts, nausea, diarrhea from mucosal ulceration of the gut, vomiting, abdominal pain, and hepatosplenomegaly. Symptoms may appear within weeks after transplant, especially involving the skin, liver, and gastrointestinal tract, or later, up to several years after transplant.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Heart, lungs, and kidneys are not the organs the brick identifies as targets of early GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GVHD is an attack on the recipient's organs by donor T cells; lymphoid organs are not the characteristic early targets described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neuromuscular tissues are not the described sites of early GVHD injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Joints, eyes, and pancreas are not the characteristic early targets; the pancreas is mentioned only as the target in type I diabetes, a type IV example.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 51-year-old man who received an allogeneic bone marrow transplant 3 years ago develops tight, thickened skin over his forearms. Biopsy shows a sparse lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermal-epidermal junction, a thinned epidermis, and thickened collagen bundles in the dermis. Which of the following best describes these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic graft-versus-host disease with epidermal atrophy and dermal sclerosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acute graft-versus-host disease with patchy epithelial cell death

choices.label: C
choices.text: Type I hypersensitivity with dermal edema

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chronic rejection with intimal smooth muscle proliferation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Type III hypersensitivity with immune-complex vasculitis

explanation.summary: Chronic GVHD of the skin shows a sparse junctional lymphocytic infiltrate, thinned epidermis (atrophy), and thickened dermal collagen (sclerosis).
explanation.whyCorrect: GVHD symptoms can appear later, up to several years after transplant. In chronic GVHD of the skin there is a sparse lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermal-epidermal junction, the epidermis is thinned, signifying atrophy, and the underlying dermis shows thickening of collagen bundles, indicative of sclerosis, which explains the tight, thickened skin.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Acute GVHD shows patchy epithelial cell death with dermal infiltrates of lymphocytes and macrophages, appearing within weeks, not epidermal atrophy with sclerosis years later.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Type I hypersensitivity produces vasodilation, edema, and smooth muscle contraction from mast cell mediators, not collagen thickening.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intimal smooth muscle proliferation is graft arteriosclerosis in chronic rejection of a solid organ, not a skin lesion after marrow transplant.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immune-complex deposition is a type III mechanism; GVHD is a type IV, T-cell mediated process without immune-complex vasculitis.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman develops a maculopapular rash, watery diarrhea, and jaundice 5 weeks after an allogeneic bone marrow transplant for leukemia. A diagnosis of graft-versus-host disease is made. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Surgical removal of the transplanted tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Transfusion of additional donor T cells

explanation.summary: Immunosuppressive drugs are used both to prevent and to treat GVHD.
explanation.whyCorrect: GVHD results from donor T cells attacking the recipient's organs, producing rash, diarrhea, and jaundice. Immunosuppressive drugs are used to both prevent and treat GVHD, as the case discussion emphasizes that medications to suppress the immune system help mitigate this risk after bone marrow transplant.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Removing the graft is the management of a hyperacutely rejected solid organ; transplanted marrow cannot be surgically removed, and the patient depends on it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Donor T cells are the cells causing GVHD; infusing more would worsen the attack on her tissues.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antibiotics address the infection risk of immunosuppressed patients but do not treat the T-cell mediated organ injury of GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Conditioning chemotherapy is given before transplant to eradicate the recipient's marrow; it is not a treatment for established GVHD.

questions.topicName: Diseases of the Immune System: Transplant Rejection

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man has long-standing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. Endoscopic biopsies are obtained. A duodenal biopsy shows a normal villous height-to-crypt ratio of 3:1. A biopsy of the sigmoid colon shows collections of neutrophils within colonic crypts and a nodular aggregation of histiocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: A nodular aggregate of histiocytes (non-caseating granuloma) in the bowel wall is the classic clue for Crohn's disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Crohn's disease is an inflammatory bowel disease that classically features nodular aggregates of histiocytes, i.e., non-caseating granulomas, and can affect any segment of the GI tract. The normal duodenal villous architecture argues against a malabsorptive enteropathy and points to a transmural granulomatous IBD.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Campylobacter jejuni causes an acute invasive enterocolitis but does not produce granulomatous inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Celiac disease produces duodenal villous atrophy with a reduced villous-to-crypt ratio; here the ratio is a normal 3:1.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clostridioides difficile causes pseudomembranous colitis without granulomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ulcerative colitis characteristically lacks granulomas and is limited to continuous mucosal disease of the colon and rectum.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman develops migratory joint pain, red and light-sensitive eyes, and painful urination about two weeks after an episode of bloody diarrhea. Which of the following pathogens was most likely responsible for her preceding gastrointestinal illness?

explanation.summary: Reactive arthritis (arthritis, conjunctivitis, urethritis) after diarrhea is a classic sequela of Campylobacter jejuni.
explanation.whyCorrect: Campylobacter jejuni infection is an important trigger of reactive arthritis, an immune-mediated triad of joint pain, conjunctivitis (light sensitivity), and urethritis (painful urination) that follows the enteric infection.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytomegalovirus can involve the eye and GI tract in immunocompromised hosts, but post-infectious reactive arthritis would be highly unusual.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Escherichia coli O157:H7 causes bloody diarrhea and may trigger hemolytic uremic syndrome, not reactive arthritis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Giardia lamblia causes malabsorption with greasy stools and is not associated with reactive arthritis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Herpes simplex virus can cause mucosal ulceration but does not classically produce reactive arthritis.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man has several months of bloody diarrhea and tenesmus. Colonoscopy shows continuous mucosal inflammation extending proximally from the rectum without intervening areas of normal mucosa. Biopsies show crypt abscesses limited to the mucosa and superficial submucosa, without granulomas. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Continuous colonic inflammation limited to the mucosa/superficial submucosa without granulomas is ulcerative colitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ulcerative colitis is limited to the colon and rectum and shows continuous involvement of the mucosa and superficial submucosa, typically with crypt abscesses and without granulomas.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Celiac disease affects the small bowel with villous atrophy, not the colon with continuous mucosal colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Crohn's disease produces skip lesions, transmural inflammation, and non-caseating granulomas rather than continuous superficial disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CMV colitis occurs in immunocompromised patients and shows owl's eye viral inclusions, not this pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Giardiasis is a small-bowel protozoal infection causing malabsorption, not a chronic continuous colitis.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman has chronic diarrhea, bloating, and iron-deficiency anemia that improve when she removes wheat, barley, and rye from her diet. Duodenal biopsy shows flattened villi with crypt hyperplasia and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes. Which of the following best explains the intestinal injury?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacterial invasion of the colonic mucosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Owl's eye viral inclusions in endothelial cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Protozoal colonization of the small-bowel lumen

explanation.summary: Celiac disease results from an immune response to gliadin (a gluten protein) that damages the duodenal mucosa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Celiac disease results from intestinal inflammation triggered by an immune response to gliadin, a constituent of the grain protein gluten, producing tissue damage and duodenal villous atrophy; symptoms resolve with gluten avoidance.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacterial mucosal invasion describes infectious colitis, not the gluten-driven small-bowel enteropathy shown here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Granulomatous inflammation is characteristic of Crohn's disease, not celiac disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Owl's eye inclusions are seen in cytomegalovirus infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Luminal protozoal colonization describes giardiasis, which does not cause immune villous atrophy responsive to gluten withdrawal.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man with biopsy-proven celiac disease develops an intensely itchy, grouped vesicular rash over the extensor surfaces of his elbows and knees. Skin biopsy with immunofluorescence shows granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillae. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Dermatitis herpetiformis is an IgA-mediated blistering skin disease associated with celiac disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dermatitis herpetiformis is a blistering, IgA-mediated condition seen in association with celiac disease when the patient develops IgA antibodies that cross-react with reticulin, a connective tissue protein; it typically involves extensor surfaces and shows granular IgA deposits.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Erythema nodosum presents as tender subcutaneous nodules on the shins, not pruritic extensor vesicles with IgA deposition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pyoderma gangrenosum forms rapidly enlarging ulcers with undermined borders, not grouped vesicles.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Psoriasis produces well-demarcated silvery-scaled plaques and lacks papillary IgA deposits.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uveitis is an intraocular inflammatory manifestation, not a skin disease.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man with AIDS and a CD4 count of 30 cells/microliter has fever, abdominal pain, and watery diarrhea. Colonoscopy shows mucosal ulcers, and biopsy reveals enlarged cells containing large intranuclear inclusions with a surrounding clear halo (owl's eye appearance). Which of the following is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Owl's eye intranuclear inclusions in an immunocompromised patient with colitis indicate cytomegalovirus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cytomegalovirus causes colitis in immunocompromised patients, and its viral cytopathic effect produces characteristic owl's eye intranuclear inclusions that are an important clue to an infectious etiology.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Campylobacter jejuni produces acute invasive enterocolitis without viral inclusion bodies.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Celiac disease is a non-infectious gluten enteropathy of the small bowel and does not produce inclusions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Escherichia coli O157:H7 causes bloody diarrhea and hemolytic uremic syndrome, not owl's eye inclusions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Giardia lamblia is a luminal protozoan causing malabsorption, not intranuclear inclusions.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man who received a kidney transplant has odynophagia and diarrhea. Endoscopic biopsy of an esophageal ulcer edge shows epithelial cells with multinucleation, nuclear molding, and margination of chromatin. Which of the following pathogens is most consistent with these findings?

explanation.summary: Multinucleation, nuclear molding, and chromatin margination are the cytopathic hallmarks of herpes simplex virus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Herpes simplex virus infection produces multinucleation, nuclear molding, and chromatin margination, and these viral cytopathic changes are an important clue to an infectious etiology, particularly in immunocompromised patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytomegalovirus produces single large owl's eye intranuclear inclusions rather than multinucleation with molding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Campylobacter jejuni is a bacterium and does not cause viral cytopathic changes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Salmonella species cause invasive enterocolitis without these nuclear inclusion features.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Giardia lamblia is a protozoan causing luminal small-bowel infection, not nuclear cytopathic effects.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl develops bloody diarrhea several days after eating an undercooked hamburger. Over the next week she becomes pale and lethargic with decreasing urine output. Laboratory studies show anemia with schistocytes, thrombocytopenia, and rising creatinine. Infection with which of the following organisms most likely triggered this complication?

explanation.summary: E. coli O157:H7 causes bloody diarrhea and can trigger hemolytic uremic syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Escherichia coli O157:H7 is an important cause of bloody diarrhea (dysentery) and may trigger hemolytic uremic syndrome, the triad of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury described here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Campylobacter jejuni is associated with reactive arthritis and Guillain-Barre syndrome, not hemolytic uremic syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytomegalovirus causes colitis in immunocompromised patients, not post-diarrheal hemolytic uremic syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Giardia lamblia causes malabsorptive, greasy diarrhea without hematologic or renal complications.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Herpes simplex virus causes mucosal ulceration, not hemolytic uremic syndrome.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man returns from a two-week backcountry camping trip where he drank from a mountain stream. He now has two weeks of bloating, foul-smelling greasy stools that float, and weight loss. Stool studies suggest malabsorption. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Greasy, foul-smelling malabsorptive stools after drinking untreated water suggest Giardia lamblia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Giardia lamblia infections result in malabsorption and greasy stools; the organism colonizes the small bowel and is classically acquired from contaminated freshwater sources.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Campylobacter jejuni causes an acute invasive, often bloody enterocolitis rather than chronic steatorrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cytomegalovirus colitis occurs in immunocompromised hosts, not in a healthy camper with malabsorption.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Escherichia coli O157:H7 causes acute bloody diarrhea and hemolytic uremic syndrome, not greasy malabsorptive stools.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Shigella species cause an acute invasive dysentery with bloody, mucoid stools, not malabsorption.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man develops rapidly progressive, symmetric ascending weakness and areflexia about three weeks after a self-limited diarrheal illness. Cerebrospinal fluid shows elevated protein with a normal cell count. A preceding infection with which of the following organisms is most classically associated with this neurologic syndrome?

explanation.summary: Guillain-Barre syndrome after diarrhea is a classic sequela of Campylobacter jejuni infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: An important potential consequence of Campylobacter jejuni infection is Guillain-Barre syndrome (along with reactive arthritis); the post-infectious immune response produces ascending paralysis with albuminocytologic dissociation in the cerebrospinal fluid.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytomegalovirus causes colitis in immunocompromised hosts and is not the classic diarrheal trigger of Guillain-Barre syndrome in this vignette.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Giardia lamblia causes malabsorption, not a post-infectious demyelinating polyneuropathy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Herpes simplex virus causes mucosal ulceration, not this ascending paralysis after enteritis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ulcerative colitis is a non-infectious inflammatory bowel disease and does not trigger Guillain-Barre syndrome.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman with a several-year history of ulcerative colitis develops fatigue, pruritus, and jaundice. Laboratory studies show a markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase, and cholangiography shows a beaded pattern of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts. Which of the following extraintestinal manifestations of inflammatory bowel disease is most likely present?

explanation.summary: Cholestasis with a beaded bile-duct pattern in an IBD patient indicates primary sclerosing cholangitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are associated with extraintestinal manifestations, including primary sclerosing cholangitis; it produces cholestatic liver disease with inflammation and fibrosis of the bile ducts, giving a beaded (strictured) appearance on cholangiography, and is most strongly linked with ulcerative colitis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ankylosing spondylitis is an axial inflammatory arthritis and would not cause cholestatic jaundice or beaded bile ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Migratory polyarthritis affects peripheral joints, not the biliary tree.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uveitis is an ocular manifestation and does not explain the hepatobiliary findings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Erythema nodosum is a skin manifestation of tender shin nodules, not a biliary disease.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A pathologist compares two resected bowel specimens from patients with inflammatory bowel disease. Specimen 1 shows patchy segments of thickened bowel wall with intervening normal areas, deep fissuring ulcers extending through all layers, and non-caseating granulomas. Specimen 2 shows continuous ulceration confined to the mucosa of the colon. Which of the following best characterizes Specimen 1?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Crohn's disease with transmural, skip-lesion inflammation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ulcerative colitis with continuous mucosal inflammation

explanation.summary: Skip lesions, transmural inflammation, and non-caseating granulomas define Crohn's disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Crohn's disease can affect any portion of the GI tract and is characterized by skip lesions, non-caseating granulomas, and transmural inflammation, exactly the pattern in Specimen 1.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ulcerative colitis, shown in Specimen 2, is continuous and limited to the mucosa/superficial submucosa without granulomas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Celiac disease affects the small-bowel mucosa with villous atrophy, not transmural granulomatous colonic disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CMV colitis is an infectious process marked by owl's eye viral inclusions, not skip lesions and granulomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Giardiasis is a luminal small-bowel protozoal infection and does not cause transmural granulomatous inflammation.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A gastroenterologist explains to a medical student that inflammatory bowel disease is a group of gastrointestinal disorders of complex pathogenesis. Which of the following pairs represents the two major disorders in this group?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Crohn's disease and Clostridioides difficile colitis

explanation.summary: The two major inflammatory bowel disorders are Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a group of gastrointestinal disorders with contributions from immune regulation, host-microbe interactions, and genetic susceptibility, and its two major forms are Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Celiac disease is a gluten-triggered enteropathy and dermatitis herpetiformis is its associated IgA-mediated skin disease; neither is classified as IBD.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ulcerative colitis is an IBD, but celiac disease is an immune response to dietary gliadin, not an inflammatory bowel disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clostridioides difficile colitis is an infectious enterocolitis, not an immune-related inflammatory bowel disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Giardiasis is a protozoal infection producing malabsorption, and celiac disease is not an IBD.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman is diagnosed with Crohn's disease. Her older brother was diagnosed with the same condition at age 19, and she asks why two siblings would develop the disease. Which of the following contributors to the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease best accounts for this family clustering?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Viral cytopathic effect in mucosal cells

explanation.summary: Genetic susceptibility is one of the recognized contributors to the complex pathogenesis of IBD.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inflammatory bowel disease has a complex pathogenesis that includes contributions from immune regulation, host-microbe interactions, and genetic susceptibility; clustering of Crohn's disease in siblings reflects the genetic component.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An immune response to gliadin is the trigger of celiac disease, not Crohn's disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Contaminated freshwater is the classic source of Giardia lamblia infection, an infectious rather than immune-related cause of diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Viral cytopathic effects (owl's eye inclusions, multinucleation) indicate cytomegalovirus or herpes simplex virus infection, not IBD.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IgA antibodies that cross-react with reticulin underlie dermatitis herpetiformis in celiac disease, not familial IBD.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man with chronic abdominal pain and diarrhea undergoes colonoscopy, which shows ulcerated segments in the terminal ileum and the ascending colon separated by normal-appearing mucosa. Which of the following additional histologic features is most likely to be present in the diseased segments?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inflammation extending through the full bowel wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Continuous involvement beginning in the rectum

explanation.summary: Skip lesions in the ileum and colon indicate Crohn's disease, which produces transmural inflammation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Crohn's disease can affect any portion of the GI tract and is characterized by skip lesions, non-caseating granulomas, and transmural inflammation; discontinuous ileal and colonic disease therefore predicts inflammation through the full thickness of the wall.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Duodenal villous flattening (villous atrophy) is the lesion of celiac disease, not Crohn's disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Inflammation limited to the mucosa and superficial submucosa is the pattern of ulcerative colitis, not Crohn's disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Owl's eye inclusions are the cytopathic hallmark of cytomegalovirus infection in immunocompromised patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Continuous involvement is characteristic of ulcerative colitis; the skip pattern here argues against it.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A pathologist examines a total colectomy specimen from a 34-year-old woman with long-standing ulcerative colitis. Which of the following best describes the expected depth of inflammatory involvement of the bowel wall?

explanation.summary: Ulcerative colitis involves the mucosa and superficial submucosa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ulcerative colitis is limited to the colon and rectum and shows continuous involvement of the mucosa and superficial submucosa, in contrast to the transmural inflammation of Crohn's disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Isolated serosal inflammation is not the pattern of ulcerative colitis, which is a mucosal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The muscularis propria is not the primary site of injury in ulcerative colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Full-thickness (transmural) inflammation characterizes Crohn's disease, not ulcerative colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ulcerative colitis stays superficial; it does not target the deep submucosa and muscularis propria.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man with a known inflammatory bowel disease develops painful swallowing. Endoscopy shows esophageal ulcers, and biopsy reveals non-caseating granulomas with no viral inclusions. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Granulomatous disease in the esophagus of an IBD patient points to Crohn's disease, which can involve any portion of the GI tract.
explanation.whyCorrect: Crohn's disease can affect any portion of the GI tract, including the esophagus, and is characterized by non-caseating granulomas, so an IBD patient with granulomatous esophageal ulcers most likely has Crohn's disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ulcerative colitis is limited to the colon and rectum and does not form granulomas, so esophageal granulomas exclude it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Celiac disease causes duodenal villous atrophy from an immune response to gliadin; it is not an IBD and does not produce granulomas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cytomegalovirus produces owl's eye intranuclear inclusions rather than granulomas.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Herpes simplex virus produces multinucleation, nuclear molding, and chromatin margination, not granulomas; no viral inclusions were seen.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man with Crohn's disease reports one year of low back pain and morning stiffness that improves with activity. Imaging shows inflammatory changes of the sacroiliac joints and spine. Which of the following extraintestinal manifestations of inflammatory bowel disease is most likely?

explanation.summary: Inflammatory axial back pain with sacroiliitis in an IBD patient is ankylosing spondylitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are known for extraintestinal manifestations including ankylosing spondylitis, an inflammatory disease of the spine and sacroiliac joints that produces chronic back pain and stiffness.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Migratory polyarthritis affects peripheral joints that change over time, not the sacroiliac joints and spine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Primary sclerosing cholangitis is a biliary manifestation and does not cause back pain or sacroiliitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uveitis is an ocular manifestation of IBD.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dermatitis herpetiformis is an IgA-mediated skin disease associated with celiac disease, not IBD.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with ulcerative colitis develops pain, redness, and light sensitivity in her left eye. She has had no recent diarrheal infection, joint symptoms, or urinary complaints. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Uveitis is an extraintestinal ocular manifestation of inflammatory bowel disease.
